checks.label: With no turns, the Activity plane discloses exactly that — no invented activity
The provider's consent request is disclosed with its actual tool call before any answer
The consent request is also activity beside the conversation, not only a composer card
Answering the card reaches the provider over the real consent wire and the turn completes
A dispatched delivery identity is inspectable with its settled owner phase — 6B's named open, closed
The Inspect plane names the stable SessionSpace ref the encounter actually lives in
The Inspect plane names the provider's actual native session identity
Owner operations are shown with the owner's own verdicts and reasons, never the desktop's
Recorded history is pointed at, not duplicated into the Context plane
The participant's operative context is disclosed as un-inspectable on this cut — never inferred from transcript or profile
The provider's actual continuation state names the native session the provider really holds
The wait row is the owner's own connection state, not a progress invention
The tool call's real payload is the activity row
The assistant's conversational reply stays in the Conversation plane — the planes do not duplicate each other
A requested stop settles as the owner's own stop record, shown verbatim — the owner journals the interruption as an error-named-Cancelled (owner finding, frozen cut)
A provider failure is disclosed as a fault, never softened into activity-as-usual
A faulted resident's seat is disclosed as held, with recovery named as the owner's — no recovery promise the owner cannot keep
The journal's raw events include the human turns on the owner's own cursor
The journal names provider events as the owner recorded them
Journal rows carry the owner's cursors, not desktop numbering
